messages:
alex_k: FYI — finished a quick bakeoff of an adaptive activation-scaling variant (act-scale) we discussed vs plain smoothquant on long-context workloads (seq ~= 96k). Compared AWQ / GPTQ / FP8 / INT8. Sending quick notes + logs. TL;DR: AWQ+act-scale looks promising (<=2% ppl delta vs fp16 on longbench), GPTQ has larger accuracy drop on code-qa (~6% EM delta), FP8 gives best latency but some hallucination/regression cases.

mina: nice, what datasets and metrics did you run? sample counts?

alex_k: ran two suites: 1) longbench-v2 synthetic long-span (8k samples, perplexity & token-level LM loss), 2) code-qa-real (QA EM + exact match, ~1.2k prompts) and a small subset of narrative-qa for rouge. Batch size 1, seq_len forced to 96000.

diego_m: how did KV cache behavior look? any memory blowups with 96k?

alex_k: KV cache growth is linear as expected. We saw one NaN path on FP8 at step ~92k tokens for the 13B model on aattle-32g; looks like activation overflow in a specific attn projection for some prompts. Nonzero for FP8 only, AWQ/INT8 stable. Log snippet:

```
RuntimeError: nan encountered in layer recv_attention_scores at step 92013
  model: redwood/long-13b
  run-id: bakeoff/1799954321/awq-fp8
```

sarah_w: can you paste the perf/quality table snapshot?

alex_k: pasted quick snapshot below (median over runs):

model | quant | ppl_delta(%) | qa_em_delta(%) | median_latency_ms | mem_gb
----- | ----- | ------------ | -------------- | ----------------- | ------
long-13b | fp16 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 2100 | 38
long-13b | awq-actscale | +1.7 | +1.2 | 1250 | 20
long-13b | gptq | +5.9 | +6.4 | 980 | 18
long-13b | fp8 | +2.5 | +3.8 | 720 | 16

notes: ppl_delta relative to fp16 (lower is better). AWQ-actscale keeps qa within 2% which is in-line with our deploy threshold; GPTQ shows larger QA regressions on code-qa.

ravi_p: did you try per-layer act-scaling vs global? which layers cause issues?

alex_k: not exhaustive yet. Initial debug shows layer 18-22 in decoder stack have high activation variance. Plan: try per-layer scale and layer-wise clipping. Quick config used:

```
quant_config = {
  'method': 'awq',
  'act_scaling': 'adaptive',
  'per_channel': true,
  'bits': 8,
  'group_size': 128
}
```

run command: `./run_long_eval.sh --model redwood/long-13b --quant awq-actscale --seq_len 96000 --batch 1`

mina: for reproductibility please upload the exact prompt seed list + python env (pip freeze). Also include the HF commit used.

alex_k: will upload; quick link: s3://redwood-bench/bakeoffs/1799954321/ (configs, seeds, logs).

bench-bot: nightly job completed — uploaded results for this run to s3://redwood-bench/bakeoffs/1799954321/summary.json :eyes:

diego_m: for deployment, I worry about FP8 NaNs in customer traffic. Suggest canary AWQ-actscale on dedicated A100-40G with KV-cache warmup and metric-based rollback.

sarah_w: what's our rollback thresholds? we have 3% EM and 5% rouge historically for model rollouts. Should we be stricter for long-context?\
mina: propose stricter: 2% QA EM and 3% ppl delta for long-context-sensitive flows. Also add spike detection for NaNs.

alex_k: agreed. Proposed rollout plan: 1) internal canary on dedicated-small (2 nodes) with 1000 synthetic longbench probes 2) 24h canary with 1% production traffic, KV cache warmup 3) auto-roll back if EM delta >2% or any NaN/error spike >0.1% of requests.

ravi_p: I'll add a per-layer scale override experiment: try `--layer_override='decoder.layers.20.act_scale=0.8'` and `--act_clip=6.0` to reduce outliers.

mina: also try mixing AWQ for MLP weights + GPTQ for attention weights (hybrid) — may keep attention numeric stability while saving memory.

alex_k: good idea. I'll run hybrid AWQ(attn->gptq) experiments tomorrow.

sarah_w: please add a short summary to the model-onboarding doc (private) so PMs know the trade-offs.

alex_k: will do. Action items: (1) upload full artifacts to S3 (alex_k) (2) run per-layer clip/scale and hybrid runs (ravi_p + alex_k) (3) schedule canary on dedicated A100-40G (diego_m) (4) update rollout thresholds and add NaN spike detector to console alerts (mina + sarah_w).

alex_k: tagging for visibility @mina @ravi_p @diego_m :eyes:

mina: thanks! excited to see if act-scale can be our default long-context quant strategy :party_parrot:
